papers.title: Debiasing hazard-based, time-varying vaccine effects using vaccine-irrelevant infections: An observational extension of a pivotal Phase 3 COVID-19 vaccine efficacy trial
papers.authors: Ethan Ashby, Dean Follmann, Holly Janes, Peter B. Gilbert, Ting Ye, Lindsey R. Baden, Hana M. El Sahly, Bo Zhang
papers.summary: The paper proposes a method to mitigate bias in time-varying vaccine effects using vaccine-irrelevant infections.
papers.main_problem: Hidden biases in time-varying vaccine effectiveness estimates obtained using Cox regression.
papers.main_contribution: A method to leverage vaccine-irrelevant infections to identify hazard-based, time-varying vaccine effectiveness in the presence of unmeasured confounding and selection bias.
papers.applications: The proposed method can be applied to provide evidence-based guidance for public health decision making.
papers.limitations: The method assumes certain conditions and may not be applicable in all scenarios.
papers.relevance_reason: The paper directly addresses the user's research topic of COVID-19 vaccine validation by proposing a method to mitigate bias in time-varying vaccine effects, making it highly relevant.

papers.title: Efficient estimation of cumulative incidence curves via data fusion with surrogates: application to integrated analysis of vaccine trial and immunobridging data
papers.authors: Pan Zhao, Peter B. Gilbert, Oliver Dukes, Bo Zhang
papers.summary: The paper proposes methods for estimating cumulative incidence curves using data from vaccine trials and immunobridging studies, with applications to COVID-19 vaccine validation.
papers.main_problem: Estimating cumulative incidence curves for vaccine trials and immunobridging studies
papers.main_contribution: Developing efficient and multiply robust estimators for counterfactual cumulative incidence curves
papers.applications: Estimating the hypothetical cumulative incidence curve for a bivalent mRNA booster, testing key assumptions of no controlled direct effects
papers.limitations: Limited to pathogens with multiple serotypes, such as dengue virus and influenza
papers.relevance_reason: The paper directly addresses the user's research topic by proposing methods for estimating cumulative incidence curves using data from vaccine trials and immunobridging studies, with applications to COVID-19 vaccine validation.

papers.title: A simple and powerful test of vaccine waning
papers.authors: Gellért Perényi, Matias Janvin, Mats J. Stensrud
papers.summary: The paper proposes a new test to assess whether vaccine efficacy wanes over time, providing a power gain over existing approaches and valid under interpretable assumptions.
papers.main_problem: Determining whether vaccine efficacy wanes over time is a subtle task, and classical approaches have limitations.
papers.main_contribution: A new formal test to assess vaccine waning, which provides a power gain over existing approaches and is valid under interpretable assumptions.
papers.applications: The proposed test can be used in vaccine trials to assess whether vaccine efficacy wanes over time, which can inform individual and public decision making.
papers.limitations: The paper does not provide a comprehensive review of existing approaches, and the new test is only illustrated through real and simulated examples.
papers.relevance_reason: The paper directly addresses the user's research topic by investigating vaccine validation, specifically the waning of vaccine efficacy over time, and proposes a new formal test to assess vaccine waning.

papers.title: Nonparametric bounds for vaccine effects in randomized trials
papers.authors: Rachel Axelrod, Uri Obolski, Daniel Nevo
papers.summary: The paper proposes nonparametric causal bounds for vaccine effects in randomized trials, addressing the issue of behavioral effects when blinding is broken.
papers.main_problem: The paper addresses the problem of estimating vaccine efficacy when blinding is broken, leading to biased estimates.
papers.main_contribution: The paper contributes nonparametric causal bounds for different types of vaccine efficacy, using linear programming-based and monotonicity-based methods.
papers.applications: The proposed bounds can be applied to vaccine trials, providing a more accurate estimate of vaccine efficacy.
papers.limitations: The paper assumes the absence of unmeasured common causes of infection risk and participants' belief about whether they received the vaccine, which may not always be the case.
papers.relevance_reason: The paper directly addresses the user's research topic of COVID-19 vaccine validation by proposing nonparametric causal bounds for vaccine effects in randomized trials.

papers.title: Sequentially Doubly Robust Estimation of Conditional Survival Probability with Time-Varying Covariates
papers.authors: Hongxiang Qiu, Marco Carone, Alex Luedtke, Peter B. Gilbert
papers.summary: The paper proposes a nonparametric estimator for conditional survival probability with time-varying covariates, accounting for censoring due to these covariates.
papers.main_problem: Estimating conditional survival probability with time-varying covariates while accounting for censoring.
papers.main_contribution: A sequentially doubly robust estimator for conditional survival probability with time-varying covariates.
papers.applications: Vaccine trials, studying the association between immune response levels and the cumulative incidence of an endpoint.
papers.limitations: The paper relies on the assumption that the censoring distribution is consistently estimated within each time window.
papers.relevance_reason: The paper's focus on conditional survival probability with time-varying covariates and its application to vaccine trials make it strongly related to the user's research topic of COVID-19 vaccine validation.
